Arbiter is a simple publish/subscribe event system for communication between modules. All instances share the same subscribers, so a module can inform others without a reference to them. import Arbiter from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Arbiter'; const subscription = new Arbiter().subscribe('ORDER/READY', (order) => console.log(order)); // Somewhere else new Arbiter().inform('ORDER/READY', { orderId: 12300, total: 100.99, }); // When the callback is no longer needed, e.g. the component is removed subscription.remove(); Method Description subscribe(event, callback) Calls the callback with the arguments of every inform(). Returns a subscription, remove() removes it. unsubscribe(event, callback) Removes the callback. inform(event, ...args) Calls the subscribers of the event. informState(event, ...args) Like inform(), and callbacks subscribed later are called right away with these arguments. clearState(event) Forgets the arguments of informState(). clearSubscribers(event) Removes all subscribers of the event. getSubscribers(event) Returns the subscribers of the event. An error thrown by a subscriber doesn't stop the others. It's rethrown asynchronously, so it still shows in the console.

An event that happens once, like "the user is logged in", is easy to miss: a module that subscribes after it was informed would wait forever. Inform it with informState() instead, and later subscribers are called right away with the last arguments: new Arbiter().informState('USER/LOGGED_IN', user); // Later, e.g. in a module loaded afterwards new Arbiter().subscribe('USER/LOGGED_IN', (user) => greet(user)); // called right away Combined with ServerJS, the server can inform your modules too: OrderEvents.js import Arbiter from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Arbiter'; export default { ready(order) { new Arbiter().inform('ORDER/READY', order); }, }; $response->bigPipe()->require("require('OrderEvents').ready()", [$order]);

AsyncRequest sends a request to an endpoint that responds with the BigPipe response format. The DOM operations and modules of the response are applied automatically, before your handler is called. import AsyncRequest from 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest'; const request = new AsyncRequest('/ajax/remove.php') .setMethod('POST') .setData({ id: 123 }) .setHandler((response) => { console.log(response.payload); }) .send(); // Cancel the request if it's no longer needed request.abort();

All setters return the request, so they can be chained. Method Description setURI(uri) The URL to call. It can also be passed to the constructor. setMethod(method) The HTTP method, POST by default. setData(data) An object (sent URL-encoded, nested objects as a[b]=c, null as an empty value, booleans as 1 and 0, undefined and empty arrays left out) or a FormData. setRequestHeader(name, value) Adds a request header. setRelative(element) The element that sent the request, see relative targets. setStatusElement(element) The element gets the status class while the request is running. setStatusClass(className) The status class, async-saving by default. send() Sends the request and returns the XMLHttpRequest. abort() Aborts the request. abandon() Aborts the request without calling its handlers, except the finally handler. setOption(name, value) Sets an option, see retries. setAllowCrossPageTransition(allow) Lets the request outlive its page, see below. Every request is sent with the X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest header and a __req parameter with a counter of the requests made from the page. A page transition abandons the requests of the page it leaves, so their responses never reach the next page. A request that must outlive its page, e.g. one that saves something in the background, calls setAllowCrossPageTransition(true).

Method Called setInitialHandler(fn) Right before the request is sent. setPreResponseHandler(fn) With the parsed response, before its DOM operations, pagelets and modules are applied. Returning false drops the response. setHandler(fn) With the parsed response, after its DOM operations and modules were applied. setErrorHandler(fn) With the XMLHttpRequest and the error when the request failed. setTransportErrorHandler(fn) Instead of the error handler, for failures without a BigPipe response: http, invalid_response, network and timeout errors. setFinallyHandler(fn) With the XMLHttpRequest after the request finished, successfully or not. setUploadProgressHandler(fn) With the upload ProgressEvent (loaded and total bytes) while the data is sent, e.g. a file. setTimeoutHandler(ms, fn) When there is no response in ms milliseconds: the request is aborted and fn gets a timeout error, or the transport error handler without fn.

When a response without an error has been handled, a success event bubbles from the relative element of the request, e.g. the link or form of the Primer, with the response as event.detail.response. For a streamed response it is dispatched with the last part. Listen to it on the element or any element above it: form.addEventListener('success', ({ detail }) => console.log(detail.response.payload));

The error handler gets the XMLHttpRequest and an error object, the same for every kind of failure: new AsyncRequest('/ajax/save') .setErrorHandler((xhr, error) => { if (error.isTransient) { // e.g. offer to try again } showMessage(error.summary, error.description); }) .send(); Property Description type Why the request failed, one of ERROR_TYPE exported by AsyncRequest, see below. code The code the server sent, or the HTTP status for http errors. status The HTTP status, 0 when there is no response. summary A short title of the error. description A sentence for the user. isWarning The server marked the error as a warning. isTransient Trying again may help: network errors, timeouts, 5xx and 429 statuses, or as the server marked it. payload The payload of a server error, null otherwise. server: the server sent an error with $response->setError(). The DOM operations and modules of the response are applied anyway, e.g. to mark an invalid field. http: the server answered with a 4xx/5xx status. invalid_response: the response is not a BigPipe response, e.g. a PHP fatal error page. network: there is no response, e.g. the browser is offline. timeout: there was no response in time, see setTimeoutHandler().

Requests without an error handler pass their errors to the default one, e.g. to show them in a dialog: import AsyncRequest from 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest'; import Dialog from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Dialog'; AsyncRequest.setDefaultErrorHandler((xhr, error) => { new Dialog().showFromModel({ title: error.summary, body: error.description }); });

A request with the retries option is sent again right away when it fails with a network error, e.g. a dropped connection, as many times as the option says. The handlers are called once, for the last attempt. HTTP errors, invalid responses and timeouts are not retried. new AsyncRequest('/ajax/feed') .setMethod('GET') .setOption('retries', 2) .send(); Retry only requests that are safe to send twice, like GET requests: the server may have handled a request whose response was lost.

With the stream option, the request sends the __stream parameter, and the server can answer in parts, e.g. every pagelet as soon as it is rendered, see AsyncResponse::stream() in the PHP library. Every part is a response of its own: it is applied, and the pre-response handler and the handler (or the error handler) are called with it, as soon as it arrives. is_first and is_last of the response tell which part it is; the finally handler is called once, at the end. new AsyncRequest('/ajax/search') .setMethod('GET') .setOption('stream', true) .setHandler(response => { if (response.is_last) { spinner.hide(); } }) .send(); A server that doesn't stream sends a single response, with both is_first and is_last. A request whose response started arriving is not retried. The parts arrive over the same XMLHttpRequest, so CSRF tokens, timeouts and abandoning work as usual. See how it works for the format.

When the server defines the CSRFToken module, e.g. with BigPipe::setCSRFToken() in PHP, every request that can change data (not GET, HEAD or OPTIONS) sends the token, but only to URLs of the same origin: { "define": [["CSRFToken", {"token": "...", "header": "X-CSRF-TOKEN", "param": null}]] } header: the request header with the token, unless the request sets this header itself. param: the field of the data with the token. A later response that defines the module again replaces the token. Without the module, add the token yourself: const token = document.querySelector('meta[name=csrf-token]').getAttribute('content'); new AsyncRequest('/ajax/save') .setRequestHeader('X-CSRF-TOKEN', token) .send();

Bootloader loads the stylesheets and scripts of the page: the CSS and JS of the pagelets and of the modules the server calls. Every file is loaded once, also when two pagelets or two names point to it, and a <link rel="stylesheet"> or <script src> already on the page is not loaded again. With a Content Security Policy, the elements get the nonce of the page.

The server can name its files in a resource map, e.g. to send short names instead of long URLs with content hashes. A pagelet or a response carries the map in resource_map, and its css and js can then use the names: { "id": "feed", "css": ["feed.css"], "js": ["feed.js"], "resource_map": { "feed.css": {"type": "css", "src": "/static/feed.1a2b3c.css"}, "feed.js": {"type": "js", "src": "/static/feed.4d5e6f.js"} } } A name keeps the first resource it was given. Anything that is not a name in the map is a URL.

import Bootloader from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Bootloader'; Bootloader.setResourceMap({ 'editor.css': { type: 'css', src: '/static/editor.css' } }); Bootloader.loadResources(['editor.css', '/static/editor.js'], () => openEditor()); loadResources(names, callback, type) calls back once all the resources are loaded, right away when they already are. A resource that fails to load counts as loaded, so one broken file does not stop the page. A URL that is not in the map is loaded as the given type, or by its extension (.css as a stylesheet, anything else as a script). Scripts run in the order they were added.

A module that the page rarely needs, like an editor, does not have to be in the bundle of the page. The server lists the resources it needs in bootloadable, with a pagelet or a response, and ServerJS loads them before it calls the module: { "resource_map": { "editor.css": {"type": "css", "src": "/static/editor.css"}, "editor.js": {"type": "js", "src": "/static/editor.js"} }, "bootloadable": {"Editor": ["editor.css", "editor.js"]}, "jsmods": {"require": [["Editor", "open", [{"__e": "post"}]]]} } The script has to make the module available when it runs, e.g. a chunk of the bundle that calls registerModules() from bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry. The other module calls of the response do not wait for it. requireLazy(modules, callback) does the same in JavaScript: it loads the resources of the bootloadable modules and calls back with the modules. Modules that are not bootloadable are required right away. import { requireLazy } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Bootloader'; button.addEventListener('click', () => { requireLazy(['Editor'], Editor => Editor.open(textarea)); });

ifRequired(name, whenLoaded, whenMissing) calls whenLoaded with the module if it is loaded already, and whenMissing otherwise, without loading anything. It returns what the callback returns. A bootloadable module is loaded once all its resources are, any other module when the module loader finds it. import ifRequired from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ifRequired'; ifRequired('Editor', Editor => Editor.save(), () => console.log('The editor was never opened.')); requireDeferred(name) is a reference to a module that is loaded later. Pass it around instead of the module, and resolve it when you need it: import requireDeferred from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/requireDeferred'; const editor = requireDeferred('Editor'); editor.preload(); // preloads the resources while the network is idle editor.getModuleIfRequired(); // the module, or undefined while it's not loaded editor.load().then(Editor => {}); // loads the resources, rejects if the module can't be required editor.loadImmediately(Editor => {}); // the same with a callback editor.onReady(Editor => {}).remove(); // calls back once it's loaded, `remove()` stops waiting requireCond(condition, whenTrue, whenFalse) requires the module named by the branch that matches, so a page can pick between two implementations without requiring both: import requireCond from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/requireCond'; const Chart = requireCond(window.matchMedia('(max-width: 600px)').matches, 'SparkLine', 'FullChart');

documents.t: A pagelet waits for its css before it is displayed, and for its js before it runs its onload jsmods. With a resource map it can split its resources further: displayResources: what the pagelet needs to be displayed, e.g. its stylesheet. allResources: everything else, e.g. the stylesheet of a dialog it opens or its scripts. They load when the JS of the pagelets loads, and the pagelet runs its onload jsmods once they are loaded. { "id": "feed", "displayResources": ["feed.css"], "allResources": ["dialog.css", "feed.js"], "resource_map": { "feed.css": {"type": "css", "src": "/static/feed.css"}, "dialog.css": {"type": "css", "src": "/static/dialog.css"}, "feed.js": {"type": "js", "src": "/static/feed.js"} } } A stylesheet in allResources does not delay the display of the pagelet.

A bootloadable module with a priority above 0 is preloaded with <link rel="preload"> while the network is idle, higher priorities first, so that it loads fast when the server or requireLazy() calls it. Its scripts run once the browser is idle. { "bootloadable": { "Dialog": {"resources": ["dialog.css", "dialog.js"], "priority": 2}, "Editor": ["editor.css", "editor.js"] } } Bootloader.preloadModules(['Dialog']) preloads the resources of modules right away, e.g. when the user hovers the button that opens the dialog. A pagelet can also prefetch what the user is likely to need next: its prefetchRsrcs load as soon as it arrives, and its prefetchJsmods run once they are loaded. { "id": "feed", "prefetchRsrcs": ["composer.js"], "prefetchJsmods": {"require": [["Composer", "warmUp"]]} }

Dialog shows modal dialogs with modal-vanilla, which uses the same markup and classes as Bootstrap modals. Dialogs can be stacked: each new one is shown above the previous one and Esc closes only the topmost. The server usually opens dialogs with DialogResponse, see Dialogs API. You can also open them from JavaScript.

Builds the dialog from a title, body and footer: import Dialog from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Dialog'; new Dialog().showFromModel({ title: 'Dialog title', body: 'html content', footer: '', controller: 'ModalLogger', backdrop: 'static', });

Shows a dialog from your own markup, the content of .modal: new Dialog().render({ content: `
...
`, dialogClassName: 'modal-lg', });

Option Default Description controller A module name or a function called with the dialog, see below. backdrop true false for no backdrop, 'static' for one that doesn't close it. keyboard true Close the dialog with Esc. animate false Animate showing and hiding. transition 0 Duration of the dialog transition in ms. backdropTransition 0 Duration of the backdrop transition in ms. timeout Show the dialog after this many ms. The method then returns a Promise. autoFocus true Move the focus into the dialog when it is shown, see Layer behaviors. trapFocus true Keep Tab inside of the dialog. refocus true Give the focus back to the element that opened the dialog when it closes. causalElement The element to give the focus back to. The focused element when the dialog is shown by default. hideOnTransition true Close the dialog before a page transition. hideOnSuccess false Close the dialog when a request sent from inside of it succeeds: true for any, or a selector for the elements that sent it. position false Set the top margin of the dialog: true, or { top, centered, ignoreTopInShortViewport }.

A controller is called with the modal and the arguments passed to the method. Use it to react to the events of the dialog: show, shown, hide, hidden and dismiss. ModalLogger.js export default class ModalLogger { constructor(modal, ...args) { modal.on('shown', () => console.log('shown', args)); modal.on('hidden', () => console.log('hidden')); } }

Every dialog is a Layer too, available as modal.layer. The events of the modal stay as they are, the layer adds its own and the behaviors above: new Dialog().showFromModel({ title: 'Unsaved changes', body: '<form>...</form>', hideOnSuccess: true, // close it when the form was saved controller: modal => { modal.layer.subscribe('beforehide', () => formIsDirty()); // return false to keep it open } }); hideOnSuccess listens to the success event of requests whose link or form is inside of the dialog. modal.hide(), the close button, a click on the backdrop and Esc all go through layer.hide(), so beforehide can keep the dialog open for all of them.

The markup and the classes (modal, modal-dialog, modal-backdrop, fade, ...) are those of modal-vanilla, compatible with Bootstrap. Your own CSS, or another framework, can style them, and Modal.templates of modal-vanilla/lib/modal replaces the markup. The layer only adds behaviour: it does not add classes, and sets the top margin of the dialog only when you ask for position.
const dialog = new Dialog(); dialog.closeCurrent(); // the topmost dialog dialog.close(2); // the last two dialogs dialog.close(); // all dialogs
The helpers that the DOM operations are built on. Use them to change the page from your own modules the same way the server does.

import DOM from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/DOM'; const list = document.querySelector('ul.logs'); DOM.appendContent(list, '
  • appended line
    • '); Method Description setContent(node, html) Replaces the content of the node. appendContent(node, html) Inserts HTML as the last child. prependContent(node, html) Inserts HTML as the first child. insertAfter(node, html) Inserts HTML after the node. insertBefore(node, html) Inserts HTML before the node. replace(node, html) Replaces the node with HTML. morph(node, html) Updates the node to match the HTML, keeping the elements that stay. morphContent(node, html) Like morph(), for the children of the node only. remove(node) Removes the node. empty(node) Removes all children of the node. caution The HTML is inserted as is. Escape any user input on the server.

replace() and setContent() throw the old elements away, so focus, typed text, scroll positions and the state of your modules are lost. morph() and morphContent() change only what differs: the elements that stay are the same DOM nodes, with their attributes and text updated. They use the morph algorithm of Alpine and Livewire, adapted from @alpinejs/morph (MIT) and shipped with this package, without a dependency. Elements are matched by their position and tag. Give the items of a list a key attribute or an id to keep them when they are reordered, added or removed. Render the same markup, including whitespace, that the page was rendered with, e.g. the same template. morph() needs HTML with a single root element. Other HTML, e.g. an empty string, replaces the node. A value typed into an input is kept, the value attribute only changes its default. Attributes with @ in their name, like @click, are supported. The Alpine integration of @alpinejs/morph is left out, so the state of Alpine components in the morphed HTML isn't kept.

Find the closest ancestor of a node, including the node itself: import { byTag, byClass, byAttribute, find } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Parent'; byTag(event.target, 'a'); byClass(event.target, 'card'); byAttribute(event.target, 'data-id'); find(event.target, (node) => node.dataset?.id === '123');
A shortcut for document.getElementById(): import $ from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/$'; $('chart').classList.add('ready');

Form reads the values of a form and locks its controls. It follows what the browser would submit: disabled controls, unchecked checkboxes and radio buttons, and buttons are left out. import Form from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Form'; Form.serialize(form); // { title: 'Hello', tags: ['a', 'b'], user: { name: 'Jo' } } Form.serialize(form, submitButton); // with the name and value of the button that submitted it Form.createFormData(form, submitButton); Form.hasFiles(form); // whether a file is chosen Form.setDisabled(form, true); // disable every control, and later enable the same ones Form.focusFirst(form); // the first field, else the first button

Fields named a[b] become objects and fields named a[] become arrays, the way PHP reads them, so what you send with AsyncRequest matches $_POST. A repeated plain name keeps its last value, as in PHP. Files are not part of the result: use createFormData() for them. // <input name="tags[]" value="a"> <input name="tags[]" value="b"> <input name="user[name]" value="Jo"> Form.serialize(form); // { tags: ['a', 'b'], user: { name: 'Jo' } }

Form.setDisabled(form, true) disables the controls and remembers which ones were disabled already. false enables only the controls it disabled itself, so a control that was disabled for another reason stays disabled. It accepts any element that holds controls, not only forms. A control that is disabled is not part of what is submitted, so read the values first. The Primer makes the controls of an async form read-only instead while it is saving, which keeps them in the tab order.

FormMonitor tracks whether a form has unsaved changes. While the form is dirty, leaving the page asks the user first: before a page transition with confirm(), and before the page is closed or reloaded with the prompt of the browser, both through Run.onBeforeUnload(). import FormMonitor from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/FormMonitor'; const monitor = new FormMonitor(document.getElementById('post-form'), { message: 'You have unsaved changes.', // or a function that gets the form, the default warn: true // false only tracks, without asking }); monitor.subscribe('dirty', () => saveButton.disabled = false); monitor.subscribe('clean', () => saveButton.disabled = true); The form is clean when it is created. It becomes dirty when the values of its fields differ from that state (the fields, checkboxes, selects and files that would be submitted), and clean again when they are changed back or the form is reset. Method Description subscribe(event, callback) change (after every edit), dirty and clean (when the state changes). Returns { remove() }. isDirty() Whether the form has unsaved changes. reset() Takes the current values as the saved state, e.g. after saving without a form submit. destroy() Stops monitoring. Done automatically when the pagelet or canvas that holds the form is destroyed, or the page is left.

A form with rel="async" (see the Primer) becomes clean when its request succeeds, see the success event. If the request fails, it stays dirty. A form that is submitted normally becomes clean when it is submitted, so the page that follows is not asked about it. A submit that is cancelled by another handler leaves the form dirty.

The module is created with the form, so the server can start monitoring it: $response->call('bigpipe-util/dist/core/FormMonitor', null, [ dobronBigPipeTransportMarker::element('post-form'), ['message' => 'Leave without saving the post?'], ]);

bigpipe-util is the JavaScript runtime of BigPipe. It sends requests, applies the DOM operations the server responds with and calls the JavaScript modules the server asks for. The server side is usually bigpipe-php, but any backend that speaks the response format works.

A bundler, such as webpack or Vite. bigpipe-util ships both ES modules and CommonJS and doesn't depend on a specific bundler. Loading your own modules by name is up to your application, see step 2. A backend that answers with BigPipe responses, e.g. richarddobron/bigpipe for PHP 8.0+.
npm install bigpipe-util

In your entrypoint (e.g. resources/js/app.js), start the Primer and tell BigPipe how to load your modules. The server refers to them by name, e.g. require('UserLoggedInAlert'), and BigPipe calls the loader to get the module. The loader has to return the module itself (its default export) synchronously. webpack resources/js/app.js import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; import { setModuleLoader } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry'; Primer(); setModuleLoader(modulePath => require('./' + modulePath).default); Vite resources/js/app.js import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; import { setModuleLoader } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry'; Primer(); // Eager, because modules are called synchronously. The entrypoint itself is excluded. const modules = import.meta.glob(['./**/*.js', '!./app.js'], { eager: true }); setModuleLoader(modulePath => modules[`./${modulePath}.js`]?.default); Any name is loaded relative to the entrypoint, so require('UserLoggedInAlert') on the server loads resources/js/UserLoggedInAlert.js. Names can contain folders, e.g. Admin/Panel. A loader that returns nothing for a name makes BigPipe throw module "..." was not found. Modules of this package are resolved automatically. The server may refer to them as bigpipe-util/src/... (or bigpipe-util/dist/...); you don't need to handle them in the loader. setModuleLoader() also defines window.require, which the inline script in the next step uses. Pass { global: false } as the second argument to prevent it. Single modules can be registered under an exact name with registerModules({ Name: module }). They win over the loader.

Dialogs use modal-vanilla, which imports the Node.js module events. Vite doesn't polyfill Node.js modules for the browser, so loading fails with Class extends value [object Object] is not a constructor or null. Install the npm package of the same name and point the import to it (the trailing slash selects the package instead of the Node.js module): npm install events vite.config.js export default defineConfig({ resolve: { alias: { events: 'events/' } } }); Restart Vite with --force to rebuild its dependency cache. webpack 5 picks the events package up on its own when it's installed.

Defining window.require yourself still works when no loader is set, so existing setups don't have to change. The loader above replaces the bigpipe-util/ branch of the old function: you only write the part for your own modules.

At the end of the page, print the script that sends the pagelets and the modules required during the page render to the browser. With PHP it's one line, and the entrypoint has to be loaded by then, so add it with a classic <script src> before it: layout.php <?= \dobron\BigPipe\BigPipe::render() ?> When the entrypoint is a deferred <script type="module">, as Vite adds it, pass the modules to ServerJS yourself once DOMContentLoaded fires. This does not send pagelets: layout.php <script> document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/ServerJS"))).handle(<?=json_encode(\dobron\BigPipe\BigPipe::jsmods())?>); }); </script> Vite adds your entrypoint as <script type="module">, and module scripts are deferred: they run after the HTML is parsed, so an inline script at the end of the page would run before window.require exists. Module scripts run before DOMContentLoaded, so this works with every bundler.
documents.s: 3. Handle the modules of the first page load

documents.t: Some warnings (e.g. a DOM operation that matches nothing) are logged only when __DEV__ is defined and truthy. In webpack define it with DefinePlugin, in Vite with define: vite.config.js export default defineConfig({ define: { __DEV__: JSON.stringify(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') } });

A module is a default export: a function, a class or an object. resources/js/MyModule.js export default class MyModule { init(...args) { console.log('Hello world!', args); } } Call it from the server: $response = new \dobron\BigPipe\AsyncResponse(); $response->call('MyModule', 'init', [ 'first argument', 'second argument', ]); $response->send();
Make links and forms asynchronous with the Primer. Send requests from your code with AsyncRequest. Learn what the server sends back in How it works.

BigPipe moves the decision about what happens on the page to the server. The browser only sends a request, the server answers with a list of instructions and bigpipe-util executes them. The user clicks a link or submits a form handled by the Primer, or your code sends an AsyncRequest. The server responds with DOM operations (domops) and JavaScript modules to call (jsmods). AsyncResponse applies the DOM operations, then ServerJS loads and calls the modules.

A response is JSON prefixed with the for (;;); shield. The shield makes the response unusable when it's loaded with a <script> tag from another site; AsyncRequest strips it before parsing. The server sends it as application/json with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so the browser never runs it as a script either. for (;;);{"payload":null,"domops":[...],"jsmods":{"require":[...]},"__ar":1} Key Description payload Custom data for your handler, see setPayload() on the server. domops DOM operations, applied in order. pagelets Optional pagelets, handed to BigPipe after the DOM operations, e.g. a pagelet loaded lazily or refreshed. jsmods Modules to call, see ServerJS. __ar Marks the response as an async response. The whole response object is also passed to the handler set with setHandler().

A streamed response is a series of parts, each followed by the delimiter /*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/. A part is JSON with a response as content and finished on the last part: {"content":{"payload":{"title":"Feed"},"domops":[...],"jsmods":{"define":[...]}},"finished":false}/*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/ {"content":{"pagelets":[{"id":"feed",...}]},"finished":false}/*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/ {"content":{"pagelets":[{"id":"__bigpipe_last","is_last":true,...}],"jsmods":{"require":[...]}},"finished":true}/*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/

Each operation is an array [type, selector, targetRelative, content]: ["appendContent", "ul.logs", false, {"__html": "
  • appended line
    • "}] type: one of setContent, appendContent, prependContent, insertAfter, insertBefore, replace, morph, morphContent (see morphing), remove, hide, show and eval (deprecated: a Content Security Policy without 'unsafe-eval' blocks it, call a module with jsmods instead). selector: a CSS selector of the element to change. targetRelative: when true, the operation targets the element that sent the request (the clicked link or the submitted form), or the element matching selector inside it. The PHP library sets it when the selector is empty. content: HTML wrapped in the __html transport marker, or JavaScript code for eval, which runs with this bound to the element. Operations whose selector matches nothing are skipped. With __DEV__ defined and truthy (see Getting started), an error is logged to the console.

AsyncRequest hands every successful response to AsyncResponse. You can use it directly to process a response you received in another way, e.g. over a WebSocket: import AsyncResponse from 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncResponse'; socket.addEventListener('message', ({ data }) => { new AsyncResponse().handle(JSON.parse(data)); });

Layer is the base of everything that floats above the page: a menu, a tooltip, a dialog. It shows and hides a DOM element, tells what happens through events, and gets its behaviour from behaviors that you enable per layer. It does not depend on a CSS framework: it sets no class names and only the inline styles it needs to work, so the element can be styled with Bootstrap, Tailwind or your own CSS. import Layer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/Layer'; const layer = new Layer('
Menu
', { classNames: ['shadow-lg'], // added to the root, with any classes of your own attributes: { role: 'menu' }, causalElement: button, // what opened it insertParent: document.body, // where the root is put when it's shown, the body by default behaviors: [HideOnEscape] }); layer.show(); layer.hide(); layer.destroy(); // removes the root and disables the behaviors The first argument is a DOM element or an HTML string with a single root element. A root that is hidden is hidden with display: none while the layer is not shown.

Subscribe with layer.subscribe(name, callback), or an array of names. The callback gets the data of the event and the name of the event, and remove() of the returned subscription unsubscribes. A callback that returns false stops what the event is about, where it says so. Event When beforeshow The layer is about to be shown. show It is shown. aftershow It is shown and positioned. beforehide hide() was called, with the source. Returning false keeps the layer open. starthide The layer starts to hide. Returning false postpones it: call finishHide() when ready, e.g. after a fade. hide It is hidden. destroy It is destroyed. key A key was pressed while it is open, with the KeyboardEvent, topmost layer first. Returning false handles the key. blur The user clicked outside of the layer, with { target }. Returning false stops it from reaching the layers below. Layer.subscribe(name, callback) listens to show, hide and destroy of all layers, with the layer as the data. Layer.getTopmostLayer() is the layer that was shown last, and Layer.getLayerOf(element) the layer of a root. A click counts as a click outside only when the mouse was pressed and released on the same element outside of the layer and of the layers opened from inside it (their causalElement is inside it).

A behavior is a class with a constructor that gets the layer, and enable() and disable(). Pass them in behaviors, or use layer.enableBehaviors([...]) and layer.disableBehaviors([...]). Every behavior is enabled once per layer. class LogOnShow { constructor(layer) { this.layer = layer; } enable() { this.subscription = this.layer.subscribe('show', () => console.log('shown')); } disable() { this.subscription.remove(); } }

The hide() of a layer takes the source of the request, one of HideSources (blur, escape, transition), which beforehide and starthide get as their data. Behavior Does HideOnEscape Hides the topmost layer when Esc is pressed, and handles the key. HideOnBlur Hides the layer on a click outside of it. Layers below stay open. HideOnTransition Hides the layer before a page transition. Override isTransitionRelevant({ from, to }) to hide only for some. DestroyOnHide Destroys the layer after it was hidden. RemoveOnHide Removes the root from the page when the layer is hidden. show() puts it back. import Layer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/Layer'; import HideOnBlur from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/HideOnBlur'; import HideOnEscape from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/HideOnEscape'; new Layer(menuElement, { behaviors: [HideOnBlur, HideOnEscape] }).show();

Behavior Does AutoFocus Moves the focus into the layer when it is shown: to the element with autofocus, else the first control (not a link), else the root. A control inside that already has the focus keeps it. TabIsolation Keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside of the topmost layer. RefocusOnHide Gives the focus back to the causalElement, or else the element that had it before the layer was shown, when the focus was in the layer. focusWithinLayer(element) from core/layer/focusWithinLayer is the focus logic of AutoFocus, and getTabbable(element) lists the elements Tab reaches.

FadeOnShow and FadeOnHide fade the root with an inline opacity transition, so they work with any CSS. They take 100 and 150 ms, and FadeOnShow.forDuration(300) and FadeOnHide.forDuration(300) return behaviors with another duration. Users who prefer reduced motion get no animation. FadeOnHide postpones the hiding with starthide and calls finishHide() when the fade is over.

ModalLayer makes a layer modal: it puts a backdrop before the root, locks the scrolling of the page, centers the root and stacks modals so that the last one shown is on top, with the only visible backdrop. Combine it with HideOnBlur to hide on a click on the backdrop and HideOnEscape for Esc. import ModalLayer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/ModalLayer'; new Layer(dialogElement, { behaviors: [ModalLayer, HideOnBlur, HideOnEscape, AutoFocus, TabIsolation] }).show(); It styles the backdrop and centers the root with inline styles, so it works without any CSS. To use your own, ModalLayer.configure() returns a behavior with other options: const Modal = ModalLayer.configure({ backdropClassName: 'fixed inset-0 bg-black/50', // no default look is applied when set backdropStyle: { backdropFilter: 'blur(2px)' }, zIndex: 50, // the first modal, the next ones are 10 above center: false, // position the root with your CSS lockScroll: false }); With center: false the root has to be positioned (e.g. fixed) by your CSS for the z-index to apply.

ContextualLayer is a Layer that is positioned next to an element, for menus, tooltips and popovers. It is placed with position: absolute in the page, so insert it in the body (the default). import ContextualLayer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/ContextualLayer'; const menu = new ContextualLayer(menuElement, { context: button, // an element, or a function that returns one position: 'below', // above, below, left or right alignment: 'start', // start, center or end of the context offsetX: 0, offsetY: 4, autoFlip: true, // the other side when it doesn't fit in the viewport keepInViewport: true, behaviors: [HideOnBlur, HideOnEscape] }); menu.show(); menu.getPosition(); // the side it was placed on after flipping menu.setPosition('right'); It is positioned again while it is shown when the window is resized or scrolled and informs reposition with the side and alignment. A layer whose context is not on the page is not shown.

Dialogs are layers: DialogLayer wraps a modal-vanilla modal, keeps its events and markup, and adds the layer events and behaviors (AutoFocus, TabIsolation, RefocusOnHide, HideOnTransition, and HideOnSuccess which hides the layer when a request sent from inside succeeds, see the success event). A dialog is always shown through the modal, so it does not use ModalLayer and the fades, which the modal has built in. calculateTopMargin(height, options) from core/layer/DialogPosition is the top margin of a dialog for the position option: options.top when it is set, else a third of the free height of the window (half with centered), at least 40.

With page transitions, the links of the site load the next page into the element with the content of the page, the canvas, instead of loading the page in full. The header, the scripts and everything the page has loaded stay, so only the content of the next page and its pagelets are requested and rendered. The server turns them on for a page by calling Quickling.init() with the canvas, see Quickling in the PHP library: Quickling.init(document.getElementById('content'), { version: '2026-10-10', // a page of another version is loaded in full inactivePageRegex: '^/admin', // paths always loaded in full badRequestKeys: ['print'], // query parameters that need a full load sessionLength: 50 // after this many page transitions the next page is loaded in full });

PageTransitions takes over the clicks on the links of the page and the GET forms. A link is left to the browser when it goes to another origin, opens a new window (target), is a download, is handled by the Primer (rel="async", rel="dialog", ajaxify), has rel="external", or is clicked with a modifier key or another button than the main one. A link to a fragment of the current page only scrolls to it. PageTransitions.go(url) loads a page from JavaScript. The back and forward buttons load the page of the history entry and restore its scroll position. When a page transition can't be used, the page is loaded in full: when the page must not be handled, the request fails, or the server sends a page of another version, e.g. after a deploy.

Quickling requests the URL with GET and the parameter quickling[version]. The server responds with an AsyncResponse whose payload has: version: the version of the page, compared with the one of Quickling.init(). title: the title of the page. body_class: the class of <body>. redirect: a URL to go to instead, with a page transition, or in full with force. Before the response is applied, the pagelets in the canvas are destroyed, pagelet/destroy is informed with the canvas as root, and the canvas is emptied. Its DOM operations then fill the canvas (the element the request is relative to) and its pagelets are loaded like on a page. Only the response of the latest page transition is applied. The request is streamed: a server that sends every pagelet as soon as it is rendered shows the next page progressively, like a page streamed with BigPipe::stream(). The page transition completes once the pagelets of the last part are displayed.

A page that is left runs its leave hooks, its timers are cleared, and its requests in flight are abandoned unless they were sent with setAllowCrossPageTransition(true), see AsyncRequest: import PageTransitions from 'bigpipe-util/dist/PageTransitions'; import { setInterval } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/TimerStorage'; setInterval(refreshTimes, 60000); // cleared when the page is left PageTransitions.addBeforeLeaveHook(() => (form.dirty ? 'You have unsaved changes.' : null)); PageTransitions.addLeaveHook(() => player.stop()); Run registers the same hooks and works for full page loads too: Run.onBeforeUnload() and Run.onLeave(). core/TimerStorage has setTimeout, setInterval, requestAnimationFrame and requestIdleCallback (with their clear and cancel functions) that end with the page, and setTimeoutAcrossTransitions, setIntervalAcrossTransitions, requestAnimationFrameAcrossTransitions and requestIdleCallbackAcrossTransitions for the timers that outlive it. The plain browser functions outlive the page too.

Informed through Arbiter: Event When pre_page_transition Before a page is left, with from and to. page_transition A handler loads the next page, with its uri. onload/exit The page is left for the next one. ajaxpipe/send The request for the next page is sent. ajaxpipe/first_response The response is about to be applied. ajaxpipe/onbeforeclearcanvas The canvas is about to be emptied. quickling/response The response was applied. page_fragment_transition A link to a fragment of the page was followed. Handlers of other kinds of page transitions can be added with PageTransitions.registerHandler(handler, priority): a handler gets the URL and returns true when it loads the page.

A pagelet is an independent part of the page, like a sidebar or a feed, with its own content, CSS and JavaScript. BigPipe shows each pagelet as soon as its CSS is loaded and loads the JavaScript files of the pagelets only after all of them are displayed, so scripts never delay the content. The server renders the pagelets, see dobron\BigPipe\Pagelet in the PHP library. For every pagelet, it outputs: (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/BigPipe"))).onPageletArrive({ id: "sidebar", css: ["/css/sidebar.css"], js: ["/js/sidebar.js"], domops: [["setContent", "#sidebar", false, {"__html": "..."}]], jsmods: {"require": [["Sidebar", "init", []]]}, onload: {"require": [["SidebarChat", "connect", []]]}, onafterload: {"require": [["SidebarPrefetch", "start", []]]}, is_last: true, }); Like the inline script of ServerJS, it needs require to exist. When the entrypoint is loaded as <script type="module"> (Vite), it runs after the page is parsed. Use <script type="module"> for the inline scripts as well: they run in document order after the entrypoint, and the pagelets are displayed once the page has been parsed instead of while it streams. With a classic <script src> (webpack) the entrypoint, placed before the pagelets, makes them display progressively.

Arrive. The CSS files of the pagelet start loading through the Bootloader, which loads every file once. Display. When its CSS (and its display resources) is loaded, the DOM operations of the pagelet are applied and its jsmods are handled by ServerJS. A module of the page bundle runs right away, a bootloadable module once its files are loaded. Load JS. When the last pagelet (is_last) has arrived and all pagelets are displayed, the JS files of all pagelets start loading. A pagelet with jsNonBlock loads its JS files right after it is displayed instead. Onload. When the JS files of a pagelet are loaded, its onload jsmods are handled: the module calls that need those files. Pagelets run their onload jsmods in the order they arrived. After load. When every pagelet has run its onload jsmods and the window has loaded, the optional onafterload jsmods of the pagelets are handled. Use them for work that must not compete with the page, like prefetching or analytics. The phases are exported as BIGPIPE_PHASE and PAGELET_PHASE from bigpipe-util/dist/BigPipe. BigPipe is a singleton, so new BigPipe() always returns the same instance with the registered pagelets.

Pagelets are displayed as soon as their CSS is loaded, in any order. The server can order them, see Pagelet::setPhase() and Pagelet::displayAfter() in the PHP library: phase (default 0): a pagelet is displayed after the pagelets of a lower phase that have arrived, e.g. the content of the page in phase 0 before the sidebar and ads in phase 1. The server sends the pagelets in the order of their phases. display_dependency: the ids of the pagelets it is displayed after, e.g. a chat that needs the feed on the page. It waits for them to arrive. (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/BigPipe"))).onPageletArrive({ id: "chat", phase: 1, display_dependency: ["feed"], // ... }); The JS of the pagelets still loads only when all of them are displayed.

Every pagelet informs pagelet_event through Arbiter on each step of its lifecycle, with the event, the id of the pagelet and the time ts from performance.now(): Event When arrive The pagelet arrived. css Its CSS files start loading. css_load Its CSS files are loaded. display_start Its DOM operations are about to be applied. display It is displayed. jsstart The JS files start loading. jsdone Its JS files are loaded, its jsmods run next. onload Its jsmods have run. The times are kept in pagelet.timings and marked with performance.mark() as pagelet_<id>_<event>, so they show in the performance panel of the browser. The names are exported as PAGELET_EVENT. The page informs its own events, exported as BIGPIPE_EVENT, with the time ts: BigPipe/init when BigPipe is created, tti_bigpipe when the time to interactive is reached, all_pagelets_displayed when the last pagelet has arrived and all are displayed, and all_pagelets_loaded when all have run their jsmods. They are informed as states, so a module that subscribes later is called right away, and they are marked with performance.mark() as well. A response with pagelets informs them again. new Arbiter().subscribe('pagelet_event', ({ event, id, ts }) => { if (event === 'display') { analytics.track('pagelet_displayed', { id, ts }); } });

With a nonce-based policy, BigPipe adds the nonce of the page to the stylesheets and scripts it loads. It takes the nonce from the CSPNonce module, which the PHP library defines in the page script after BigPipe::setNonce(), or else from the first <script nonce="..."> on the page, e.g. the inline script that calls onPageletArrive.

A pagelet can be loaded later from an endpoint, e.g. a pagelet below the fold. The server prints its placeholder, the root element of the pagelet, and calls UIPagelet.loadFromEndpoint() with it, see LazyPagelet in the PHP library: UIPagelet.loadFromEndpoint('/pagelets/feed', 'pagelet_feed', { page: 2 }, { load: 'visible' }); It requests the URL with the data when the placeholder comes within 300 pixels of the viewport (visible, default), when the browser is idle (idle) or right away (load). The response puts the pagelet in the place of the placeholder, and BigPipe loads its CSS and JS like on a page. While it loads, the placeholder has the async-saving class, and errors go to the default error handler. When the pagelet the placeholder is in is destroyed, it stops waiting and aborts the request.

A list loads its next page when the user scrolls to its end. The server prints a plain "See more" link handled by the Primer and creates MorePagerFetchOnScroll with it, see MorePager in the PHP library: new MorePagerFetchOnScroll(document.getElementById('more_pager'), 300); It clicks the link when it comes within the offset of the viewport. The response appends the items and replaces the link with the one of the next page, or removes it. remove() stops waiting, and so does destroying the pagelet the link is in.

The pagelets of the first phases are the content the user is waiting for, the others are the rest of the page. The server tells which ones with tti_phase, a field of a pagelet: the time to interactive is reached when every pagelet of the phases up to it is displayed. new Arbiter().subscribe('tti_bigpipe', ({ phase, ts }) => { analytics.track('interactive', { phase, ts }); }); The event is informed once per page as a state, so a module that subscribes later is called right away. It waits until no pagelet of the phases up to tti_phase can arrive any more, i.e. a pagelet of a later phase or the last pagelet has arrived. A page transition forgets it for the next page. Right after the time to interactive, the browser downloads the js and allResources of the pagelets of the later phases in the background (<link rel="preload">), without running them. The scripts then are in the cache when the pagelets load their JS, after all of them are displayed, and nothing competes with the content of the first phases before. A pagelet of a later phase that arrives after the time to interactive is prefetched when it arrives.

A pagelet is destroyed when a pagelet with the same id replaces it, e.g. when the server refreshes it, or when the DOM operations of a response remove its root element. Destroying a pagelet destroys the pagelets inside it, runs its destructors, informs pagelet/destroy with its id and root through Arbiter and empties its root element. A module stops what it started for a pagelet in a destructor, e.g. a subscription or a timer: import BigPipe from 'bigpipe-util/dist/BigPipe'; import Arbiter from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Arbiter'; export default class Feed { init(element) { const subscription = new Arbiter().subscribe('POST/ADDED', post => this.add(post)); const timer = setInterval(() => this.refreshTimes(), 60000); new BigPipe().getPageletForNode(element)?.addDestructor(() => { subscription.remove(); clearInterval(timer); }); } } getPageletForNode() finds the pagelet an element is in, by its root element #pagelet_<id>. getRoot() returns the root of a displayed pagelet, and removePagelet(pagelet) destroys a pagelet.

A failing pagelet does not stop the page. A pagelet that fails to arrive is reported, and the next pagelets arrive as usual. When the DOM operations of a pagelet fail, the error is reported, pagelet/error is informed through Arbiter with its id and the error, and the pagelet still counts as displayed: its modules run and the JS of the page loads. Every module call is isolated too, see ServerJS. new Arbiter().subscribe('pagelet/error', ({ id }) => { document.getElementById('pagelet_' + id).classList.add('pagelet-failed'); }); Errors are reported with reportError(): they are thrown asynchronously, so they reach window.onerror and the error tracking of the page without stopping BigPipe.

Poller sends a request again and again, e.g. to check for new notifications. The next request is sent an interval after the last one finished, so slow responses never pile up. Like any AsyncRequest, the DOM operations and modules of a response are applied. The server starts a poller with a module call, see Poller in the PHP library: new Poller({ uri: '/notifications/poll', data: { since: 1728550000 }, interval: 30000 }); Option Default Description uri, method, data GET The request to send. Without uri, setupRequest sets up the request. setupRequest (request, poller) => …, sets up every request, e.g. its handler. interval Milliseconds between two requests, at least 2 seconds, or a function of the number of requests. maxRequests no limit The poller stops after this many requests and informs done. muteWhenHidden true Pauses while the page is hidden, e.g. in a background tab. muteWhenIdle 0 Pauses when the user was not active for this many milliseconds, and goes on once they are. clearOnQuicklingEvents true A page transition ends the poller. dontStart false Waits for start(). id Lets the server control the poller, see below. A poller is controlled with start(), stop(), reset(), mute(), resume(), skip() (skips the next request), setInterval(ms) and destroy(). subscribe('done', callback) is called when it stops after maxRequests.

With an id, every request of the poller sends the __poller parameter with it, and a response can call the methods of the poller as the module of that id, e.g. to poll less often or to stop: {"jsmods": {"require": [["poller_notifications", "setInterval", [60000]]]}}

The poller uses two modules that can be used on their own: core/Visibility: isHidden(), and subscribe(Visibility.HIDDEN | Visibility.VISIBLE, callback) when the page is hidden or shown. core/UserActivity: isActive(ms), whether the user scrolled, moved the mouse, clicked, typed or focused the window in the last ms milliseconds, and subscribe(callback) when they are active again.

The Primer makes links and forms asynchronous without writing any JavaScript. It registers a single click and submit listener on the document, so it also works for content added later. import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; Primer(); The Primer cancels the click or submit at once and sends the request through AsyncRequest as soon as it is available, so it can be started early and AsyncRequest loaded on demand, see Loading AsyncRequest on demand.

Add the URL to call in ajaxify and pick the behaviour with rel: Remove item rel Method Description async GET Sends the request and handles the response. async-post POST The same as async, but with POST. dialog POST Intended for requests that open a dialog. Links with a real href (other than #) still open normally when clicked with the middle mouse button or with a modifier key, so users can open them in a new tab.

Forms with rel="async" are submitted in the background. The form data, including the name and value of the button that submitted it, is sent to ajaxify or, if missing, to action, with the form's method. <form action="/ajax/subscribe.php" method="POST" rel="async"> <input name="email" type="email"> <button type="submit" name="plan" value="free">Subscribe</button> </form> While the request is running: the inputs, selects and textareas are made read-only and the submit button is disabled, unless the form has the disable-prevent-form class, an element with the form-loader class inside the form gets the loading class.

A form with rel="async" and a chosen file is sent as multipart/form-data, so PHP reads the files from $_FILES. While the data is uploaded the form reports the progress, three ways, so use what suits your markup: <form action="/upload.php" method="POST" rel="async"> <input type="file" name="photo"> <progress></progress> <!-- value and max are set, and reset when the request is over --> <button type="submit">Upload</button> </form> form.addEventListener('uploadprogress', ({ detail }) => { console.log(detail.loaded, detail.total, detail.ratio); // bubbles from the form }); form::after { content: ''; display: block; height: 4px; background: currentColor; transform: scaleX(var(--upload-progress, 0)); /* the ratio from 0 to 1 while uploading */ transform-origin: left; } Only a form with a chosen file reports progress. For your own requests use AsyncRequest.setUploadProgressHandler().

The Primer does not import AsyncRequest: it asks the Bootloader for the module bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest, which the module loader resolves like the modules the server calls (the ModuleRegistry of this package provides it). A click before the module is available is not lost and does not follow the link: it is cancelled and the request is sent the moment the module is loaded. Further clicks on the same link, or submits of the same form, are ignored in the meantime, and the data of a form is the data at the time of the submit. This lets a small entrypoint with the Primer run early, e.g. in the <head>, while AsyncRequest and the rest of the library load later: early.js import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; import Bootloader from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Bootloader'; Bootloader.setResourceMap({ 'main.js': { type: 'js', src: '/static/main.js' } }); Bootloader.enableBootload({ 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest': ['main.js'] }); Primer(); main.js is the entrypoint with import 'bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry'; once it has run, the module resolves and the waiting requests are sent. If the module can't be loaded, the error is reported and the link or form works again.

The link or form gets the async-saving class while its request is running. Clicks on a link with this class are ignored, which prevents double submits. Use it to show a spinner: .async-saving { cursor: progress; opacity: 0.6; }
The requests of links and forms have no error handler of their own, so their errors go to the default error handler, e.g. to show them in a dialog.
The link or form becomes the relative element of the request. DOM operations with an empty selector target it, see DOM operations.

Run registers callbacks for the moments of a page's life: when it is loaded, before it is left and when it is left. They work for a full page load and for a page transition alike, so the same code is right whether the user closes the tab or follows a link that loads the next page into the canvas. Every function returns a subscription, remove() unregisters the callback, and an error in a callback is reported without stopping the others. import Run from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Run'; Run.onLoad(() => init()); // the DOM is ready Run.onAfterLoad(() => prefetch()); // the window has loaded Run.onBeforeUnload(() => (dirty ? 'You have unsaved changes.' : null)); Run.onLeave(() => socket.close()); // the page is left Run.onUnload(() => navigator.sendBeacon('/log', data)); Run.onCleanupOrLeave(element, () => observer.disconnect()); Function Runs onLoad(callback) When the DOM is ready, or right away if it already is. onAfterLoad(callback) After the load event of the window, or on the next tick if it already happened. onBeforeUnload(hook) Before the page is left. The hook returns a message to ask the user first, or nothing. onLeave(callback) Once, when the page is left with a page transition, closed, reloaded or navigated away from. onUnload(callback) When the page is closed, reloaded or navigated away from (pagehide), not on a page transition. onCleanupOrLeave(element, callback) Once, when the pagelet or canvas that holds the element is destroyed, or the page is left.

onBeforeUnload() asks for confirmation before the user loses unsaved work. For a page transition the message is shown with confirm() and declining keeps the page; for a close or a reload the browser shows its own prompt, with its own text. When a page transition ends in a full page load because no handler loads the page, the user is asked once. onLeave() is the place to stop what the page started: sockets, observers, listeners on the document. Use onUnload() only for what must run when the page really goes away, like sending a beacon, as a page transition keeps the document. FormMonitor uses onBeforeUnload() to ask before a form with unsaved changes is left. onCleanupOrLeave() ties a cleanup to an element. The elements inside a pagelet are gone when the pagelet is destroyed, e.g. when a page transition empties the canvas or a response replaces the pagelet, long before the page is left: class Clock { init(element) { const timer = setInterval(() => (element.textContent = new Date().toLocaleTimeString()), 1000); Run.onCleanupOrLeave(element, () => clearInterval(timer)); } } The timers of core/TimerStorage and the requests of a page end with it without any of this, see Page transitions.

ServerJS calls the JavaScript modules that the server requires. It handles the jsmods of every response and, at the end of the page, the modules required while rendering it: <script> document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/ServerJS"))).handle(<?=json_encode(\dobron\BigPipe\BigPipe::jsmods())?>); }); </script>

jsmods.require is a list of [module, method, args]: { "require": [ ["UserLoggedInAlert", null, ["Marvin"]], ["ChartRenderer", "render", [{"__e": "chart"}, [10, 20, 30]]] ] } The module is resolved by the loader set with setModuleLoader(), see Getting started. Without a method, the module is called as a constructor with the arguments: new UserLoggedInAlert('Marvin'). An instance is only created, if it was not yet. With a method, a class is instantiated without arguments and the method is called with them: new ChartRenderer().render(element, [10, 20, 30]). A module that exports an object has the method called on the object directly. In PHP: $response->bigPipe()->require("require('UserLoggedInAlert')", ['Marvin']); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('ChartRenderer').render()", [ \dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker::transportElement('chart'), [10, 20, 30], ]);

A call with a method creates a new object of a class every time. To keep one object and talk to it from more calls, the server defines an instance in jsmods.instances, a list of [id, module, args]: { "instances": [["__inst_u_0_1", "ChartRenderer", [{"__e": "chart"}, [10, 20, 30]]]], "require": [ ["__inst_u_0_1", "render"], ["Dashboard", "add", [{"__m": "__inst_u_0_1"}]] ] } The instance is created with new ChartRenderer(element, [10, 20, 30]) the first time something requires it, by its id in require or in a __m transport marker, and every later use gets the same object, also in the following responses. In PHP: $chart = $response->bigPipe()->instance('ChartRenderer', [ \dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker::transportElement('chart'), [10, 20, 30], ]); $chart->call('render'); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('Dashboard').add()", [$chart]);

The server can send data as a module, e.g. the configuration of the page or the current user, in jsmods.define, a list of [name, exports]: { "define": [["SiteData", {"locale": "sk_SK", "user": {"id": 7}}]] } The module is required like any other, requireModule('SiteData'), or passed to a call with a __m transport marker. Its transport markers are replaced when it is required for the first time. Defines are handled before the instances and calls of the same jsmods, and a module defined again, e.g. by a later response, replaces the previous one. In PHP: $response->bigPipe()->define('SiteData', [ 'locale' => 'sk_SK', 'user' => ['id' => 7], ]);

Every define, instance and call runs on its own: when one fails, e.g. a module that doesn't exist or a method that throws, the others still run and the pagelet still finishes. The error is thrown again asynchronously, so it shows in the console and reaches window.onerror and error trackers.

Arguments are JSON, so values that JSON can't express are sent as markers and replaced before the module is called: Marker Replaced with PHP __e The element with this id. TransportMarker::transportElement() __m The module, resolved the same way as require. TransportMarker::transportModule() __map A Map created from the list of [key, value]. TransportMarker::transportMap() __set A Set created from the list of values. TransportMarker::transportSet() __html Used for the HTML content of DOM operations. TransportMarker::transportHtml() Markers are replaced at any depth of the arguments.

Calls the callback after the load event of the window, or on the next tick if the page is already loaded. import onAfterLoad from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/onAfterLoad'; onAfterLoad(() => console.log('The page is loaded.')); See Run for removable subscriptions and the hooks for leaving a page.

Calls the callback once, when the element comes within buffer pixels of the viewport, e.g. to load content right before the user scrolls to it. remove() of the returned subscription stops waiting. import onVisible from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/onVisible'; const subscription = onVisible(element, () => console.log('Almost visible.'), { buffer: 300 });
import ReloadPage from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ReloadPage'; new ReloadPage().now(); new ReloadPage().delay(250); // in ms The server calls it with $response->reload($delay).
import ServerRedirect from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ServerRedirect'; new ServerRedirect().redirectPageTo('/onboarding', 500); // delay in ms The server calls it with $response->redirect($url, $delay).

Keeps data for an element, any other object or a string namespace, without putting it on the element. The data of an element goes away with the element. import DataStore from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/DataStore'; DataStore.set(button, 'tooltip', tooltip); DataStore.get(button, 'tooltip'); DataStore.get(button, 'count', 0); // the data-count attribute of the element, or else 0 DataStore.remove(button, 'tooltip'); DataStore.purge(button); // removes all data of the element

Sets the title of the page and lets it blink, e.g. to show a new message in a background tab. Page transitions set the title with it too. import DocumentTitle from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/DocumentTitle'; DocumentTitle.set('Messages'); // informs update_title DocumentTitle.set('(2) Messages', true); // a temporary title, get() still returns 'Messages' const blinking = DocumentTitle.blink('New message'); // alternates every 1.5 seconds blinking.stop();

Keyboard shortcuts. A key is a name of KeyEventController.KEYS (ESCAPE, RETURN, SLASH, UP, ...) or a character. By default, a shortcut runs on keydown without Ctrl, Alt or Meta, and not while the user types in a text field, except navigation keys like ESCAPE in an empty one. A callback that returns false prevents the default action and stops the other shortcuts of the key. import KeyEventController from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/KeyEventController'; KeyEventController.registerKey('j', () => feed.next()); KeyEventController.registerKey('SLASH', () => { search.focus(); return false; }); const subscription = KeyEventController.registerKeyAcrossTransitions('ESCAPE', () => dialog.hide()); subscription.remove(); A page transition removes the shortcuts of the page; the ones registered across transitions stay. registerKey(key, callback, filter, replace) takes another filter (event, type) => boolean, and with replace it replaces the other shortcuts of the key.

The local and session storage, or null when the browser does not allow them, e.g. in a private window, and reads and writes that never throw. import WebStorage from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/WebStorage'; const storage = WebStorage.getLocalStorage(); // or getSessionStorage() const error = WebStorage.setItemGuarded(storage, 'draft', text); // null, or the error, e.g. a full storage const draft = WebStorage.getItemGuarded(storage, 'draft'); // null without the storage WebStorage.removeItemGuarded(storage, 'draft');

Reads and writes cookies. A cookie is set for the path / with SameSite=Lax, and Secure on HTTPS. import Cookie from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Cookie'; Cookie.set('theme', 'dark', { lifetime: 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 }); // milliseconds, a session cookie without it Cookie.get('theme'); // 'dark', or null Cookie.clear('theme'); set() also takes path, domain, secure and sameSite, and clear() takes path and domain.
